scores.reasons:
Workload: llama-bench TinyLlama Q4_K_M tg128. Metric: t/s.
- Base for every-thread and per-block rows: 67.9 t/s (1.885 s per run) with only mul_mat_vec_q probed. Per run that is 3,137,339,392 threads, 98.0M warps and 24.5M blocks of 128.
- Base for per-launch rows: the four kernels with the filter alone, 56.9 t/s (2.25 s per run), 15,616 calls per run. The 16-point filter is outside every design, so a map can win back at most 0.326 s per run.
- Tags: [M] measured in our results, [D] arithmetic on [M], [I] inferred. Empty-kernel anchors applied to mul_mat_vec_q are [M shape, I transfer].

EVERY THREAD
- Counter on a constant or pid key (cuda-counter call_count, threadhist):
  - helper-call walk 0.066-0.073 ns [D: map-lowering h1/h2's inline saving of 0.108 minus probe-cost section 7's atomic-form part, 0.035-0.042];
  - plus the add on one word, 0.99-1.10 ns [M shape, merge-cost]. The '1.0 alone' subtracts the carry-only column that the 11-17 correction flagged.
  - Total about 1.06-1.17 ns: +3.3-3.7 s per run, 24-25 t/s, -62% to -65% if it adds to the base. At least -51% if the 3.1 s of serialized adds only hides under the kernel's own ~1.2 s [I].
  - FLAG: a contended global atomic per thread on one key.
- SM keys (8 words): 0.25-0.27 [D, per-SM column] + 0.07 = about 0.33 ns, -35%.
- Warp keys: 0.275 [M shape, e2 dev: 72.1 us / 262,144] + 0.07 = about 0.35 ns, -37%.
- Variant 1534 (values sharded):
  - add 0.010-0.015 [M, addmin] + walk 0.066-0.073 [D] = at least 0.08-0.09 ns, about -12% or worse;
  - the 0.06 low end needs the inline walk that v1 defers.
- Per-block start time (start_ts, BPF_ANY of 8 B from every thread):
  - two helper calls 0.13-0.15 [D] + a strong 8-B store 0.032-0.174 [M, e2 store row] = about 0.17-0.33 ns, -22% to -36% [I];
  - it is the only design that runs this store-shaped idiom on the device.
  - Cliff: start_ts has max_entries 1,024 against 5,632 blocks per mul_mat_vec_q launch. About 82% of threads then take the E2BIG path: atom.add on `bound`, a give-back, and +1 on `e2big`. That is three RMWs on one 64-B control block, about 1 ns each [M shape]: about 2.5 ns per thread, +7.7 s, about -80% [I].
  - The same holds for thread_mapping (4,096 entries against 720,896 threads per launch) and for per-thread start times with a CPU-sized max_entries.
  - FLAG.
- Per-thread start time within capacity: 0.3-1.0 ns [I], -33% to -62%.
  - At llama scale it needs 8,388,608 slots: 128 MiB of device memory plus two mirrors and staging.
  - Each delivery then copies for about 31 ms [D, at hist's 0.24 ms/MB], against a 20 ms busy cadence. A continuous copier cost 12.2% on tg128 [M, step0 e3].
- total_time_ns (plain +=): about 0.15-0.3 ns [I]; the idiom itself loses data.
- Unpriced on every lookup: ld.acquire.gpu lowers to LDG.E.64.STRONG.GPU + CCTL.IVALL [M, step0b c4 SASS table]. That is one L1 invalidation per warp exit on a kernel whose resident warps share L1. C3(c) treats the relaxed form as informational only.

ONE PER BLOCK
- rms_norm pp32 (1,378 calls): at most 1.4 ms per run [I], against +18 ms (44%) today [M].
- mul_mat_vec_q (24.5M blocks): bounded by latency. 0.5-1 us x 24.5M / 72 resident blocks (36-warp boundary) gives up to 0.17-0.34 s, -8% to -15% [I]. The design did not price this row.

ONE PER LAUNCH
- At most 1 us x 15,616 = 16 ms [I], about 56.5 t/s, against 49.7 t/s today [M].

VERIFIED: 1.0 ns, -64%, 0.275 ns and 8.8 ns per warp, the CAS loop at 41 ns over 8 words, delivery 0.30-0.65 ms, and the memory sizes (32 KiB, 704 KiB, 4 MiB).
must_fix: Make value shards (1534) the default for adds: the unsharded hot counter costs about 1.06-1.17 ns per thread (-51% to -65%).

Read `bound` with a relaxed load before reserving, and keep the E2BIG and EEXIST counts in sharded counters. Otherwise a full table (start_ts 1,024 against 5,632 blocks; thread_mapping 4,096) puts three RMWs per thread on one control block: about 2.5 ns per thread, -80%.
Re-price the walk from the measured helper anchor (0.066-0.073 ns derived), and make the inline walk for constant fds part of v1.
Make the cost of ld.acquire.gpu (LDG plus CCTL.IVALL per warp) on mul_mat_vec_q a deciding variant in C3, not an informational one.
Price per-thread key tables at llama scale (128 MiB, about 31 ms per delivery), or send per-thread scratch to 1530 by rule up front.

scores.reasons:
Workload, base and tags as for device-table: tg128 t/s; 67.9 t/s (1.885 s per run) with mul_mat_vec_q probed; per-launch rows against the filter alone, 56.9 t/s; [M]/[D]/[I]. The hit path is inline for constant fds, uses relaxed loads only, and has no helper call and no acquire.

EVERY THREAD
- Counter on a constant, pid or SM key:
  - red.global 0.010-0.015 [M, addmin on mul_mat_vec_q] + one dependent ld.relaxed.gpu.global of the key word [not measured; the awaited-reply analog adds 0.028-0.033, M]. Total 0.02-0.06 ns [I]: +0.06-0.19 s per run, -3% to -9%.
  - Each word is hit only by its (SM, lane), 48 warps, as in 1531 [M shape: (SM, lane) 0.154-0.163 in all, empty kernels].
  - No host call and no global hot word.
  - rms_norm per thread: 705,536 x 0.05 ns = 35 us per prefill [D], against 7.92-8.15 s today [M].
- Warp keys: 48 per (SM, lane) shard, in C1 = 64 with a P1 = 8 window, which is load 0.75 [I].
  - A spilled key puts 32 lanes on one spill word: 0.275 ns [M shape, e2] + up to 8 window loads = about 0.3-0.4 ns on that share, up to -37% [I].
  - Sized for 48 keys: about 0.03-0.08 ns [I].
- Block keys from every thread: about 700 keys per shard, so they go to the spill table.
  - A block's 4 warps share each spill word: about 0.4-0.6 ns, -40% to -50% [I].
  - Cliff: at max_entries 1,024, C2 = 2,048 is below 5,632 keys per launch. A full spill table is probed in full on every miss: 8 + 2,048 dependent L2 loads, thousands of seconds per run [I]. FLAG (a cliff, not the common case).
- Store-shaped idioms (start_ts, per-thread start, thread_mapping, total_time_ns, leader BPF_ANY) are refused.
  - Rule applied to all four designs: refused = not served, priced at today's host call, which a tool that keeps HASH still pays: about 34,500 s per run at thread rate [D].

ONE PER BLOCK
- rms_norm: well under 0.1 ms [I], against +18 ms [M].
- mul_mat_vec_q: about 0.3-0.5 us of latency x 24.5M / 72 resident blocks, at most 0.1-0.17 s [I].

ONE PER LAUNCH
- At most 16 ms [I], against +0.326 s [M]. Shards buy nothing at this rate; the gain is the removed host call.

DELIVERY
- 295 KB, 0.3-1.1 ms [I from M anchors]. In-call delivery: 3-11 s per item [D]; the design flags this.

VERIFIED: 262,144 + 32,768 B, 35 us, the merge-cost table, 0.70-1.14 ps per SASS instruction, 1.3 against 82-106 ns, and about 1.0 ns for a spilled hot key. That the 0.028-0.033 is the wait for the atomic's reply is section 7's own inference.
must_fix: Bound the spill-table probe and return NULL early. Probing all C2 slots per miss is a cliff once block or thread keys exceed C2 (5,632 blocks against 2,048).
Size C1 and P1 so that 48 warp keys per (SM, lane) never spill. A spilled warp key costs about 0.3-0.4 ns per thread (-37%).
Measure the dependent ld.relaxed.gpu.global on mul_mat_vec_q before claiming 0.02-0.06 ns. It is the deciding number, and route-first depends on it too.
Price every-thread block keys (spill contention, about 0.4-0.6 ns) in the cost section.
Build the claimed-slot lists before offering in-call delivery.

scores.reasons:
Workload, base and tags as above (tg128 t/s; 67.9 t/s with mul_mat_vec_q probed; per launch against 56.9 t/s).

EVERY THREAD
- Sum cells on keys that decode (constant, pid, SM, warp):
  - decoder + ld.relaxed.gpu of the state word [not measured: the same load as shards] + an inline red.global into the lane shard. The measured anchors are 1531's map part, 0.035 [M, m1/m2], and its add, 0.010-0.015 [M]. Total 0.02-0.06 ns [I], -3% to -9%.
  - Warp keys decode to 384 cells x 32 lane shards, so no word is shared within a warp. That beats shards' default.
  - No host call and no hot word.
  - If any site uses a fetch result, S = 1: one word, about 1.06-1.1 ns, -51% to -65%. This depends on check 1 (XADD or FETCH).
- Per-thread start time (thread-private, 1530 in address form):
  - +0.025 ns over by-value [M analog: 0.150-0.152 against 0.125-0.127], so the map part is about 0.025-0.035 ns, -1% to -2%, with 16 B of local memory per thread.
  - The cheapest of the four for this idiom.
- Word cells at thread rate (total_time_ns from every thread, micro update, hostwake): a lock on one word per operation.
  - cas_sm in device memory [M]: 41-47 ns per operation over 8 words, about 8x per word, so 41-350 ns per operation [D].
  - That is +129 to +1,100 s per run, plus the acquire-side CCTL.IVALL of each seqlock read [not priced].
  - The design's 'several ns' is not anchored and is 1-2 orders too low. Still below today's 34,500-69,000 s.
  - FLAG.
- Host-call fallbacks at thread rate: start_ts (block key, every thread) and thread_mapping. Each is one host call per thread, about 34,500 s per run [D]. FLAG.

ONE PER BLOCK
- blockIdx has no bound at load time, so it falls back to the host call: rms_norm stays at +18 ms (44%) [M]; mul_mat_vec_q costs 24.5M x 11 us = 270 s [D].
- Per-block counters on a constant key are sum cells: nanoseconds.

ONE PER LAUNCH
- Sum-cell counters: at most 16 ms.
- Word cells for leader state (cudagraph, gpu_shared_map) through helpers: about 1-3 us per operation [I], at most 47 ms (2.4%), against 0.326 s [M].

DELIVERY
- Small: 2 KiB per constant key, 96 KiB for the warp histogram [D].

VERIFIED: 0.035; 0.010-0.015 against 0.061-0.069; 0.125 against 0.150; start-up 76-155 s; in-call +0.7-1.0 and +4.6-4.7 points; 29 sites.
must_fix: Re-price word cells at thread rate: 41-350 ns per operation (derived), 129-1,100 s per run. Refuse word cells for maps written by every thread, or limit them to leader-rate sites.
Add a run-time interval decoder ([0, max_entries) with an inline check), so blockIdx-keyed counters become sum cells instead of a host call per operation (270 s per run per block on mul_mat_vec_q).
Make the fetch-result liveness analysis part of v1: S = 1 turns a hot counter into about 1.06-1.1 ns per thread.
State in the cost section that the host-call fallbacks at thread rate (start_ts, thread_mapping) stay at about 34,500 s per run.
Measure the state load on mul_mat_vec_q (check 3) as the deciding number.

scores.reasons:
Workload, base and tags as above (tg128 t/s; 67.9 t/s with mul_mat_vec_q probed; per launch against 56.9 t/s). The table stays in registered memory, which the Tegra document says is not L2-cached on the Orin.

EVERY THREAD
- Counter on a constant or pid key:
  - the tool's own atomic in registered memory. 32 lanes on one word per warp cost 59.8 ns per thread [M, e2: 15,680.8 us / 262,144]. One word for all warps serializes at about 80-106 ns per operation GPU-wide [M, atom_sm reg].
  - That is +188 to +330 s per run, 0.4-0.7 t/s, -99% [D].
  - FLAG.
- SM keys: +250-330 s; warp keys: +188 s [D]. FLAG.
- Per-thread start, start_ts, thread_mapping and total_time_ns: every write and every first touch stays a host call, 1-3 per thread: 34,500-100,000 s per run [D]. FLAG.
- Validation by ld.acquire.sys on every hit: an uncached DRAM read plus, presumably, CCTL.IVALL [not priced; the c4 table has only the .gpu form]. The design's own 0.003-0.1 ns is up to 3x the 0.03 ns budget.
- The sum extension, which leaves this starting point: 0.02-0.045 ns [I], -6% to -13%, and the validation load still applies.

ONE PER BLOCK
- mul_mat_vec_q: 105-296 ns per operation [M, atom_sm reg], +2.6-7.3 s, -58% to -79% [D]. With own words, 50 ns gives 1.2 s; with red, 17.6 ns gives 0.43 s.
- rms_norm: 0.14-0.41 ms (0.6-1.8%) [D], against +18 ms [M].

ONE PER LAUNCH
- About 2-3 us per call [I], at most 47 ms, about 55.7 t/s, against 49.7 t/s today [M].
- cudagraph keeps 4 of its 7 operations per launch as host calls: 18-21 us when sparse [M], 70 us under graphs on the old base [M].

VERIFIED: every e2 figure (59.8, 50.0, 17.6, 105, 296, 0.286 against 0.056, 50.55 against 50.54) and the budget table (0.030 ns, 0.96 ns, 3.8 ns, 6.0 us).
must_fix: Every-thread and every-warp adds land on registered memory (at least 59.8 ns per thread). Make the sum extension the path for add-only maps, or claim per-launch use only.
Writes and first touches per thread remain host calls (34,500-100,000 s per run); the design has no device path for them.
Measure the cost of the ld.acquire.sys validation per warp on mul_mat_vec_q before any per-warp or per-thread claim.
State that per-block use is limited to light kernels: mul_mat_vec_q pays +2.6-7.3 s per run.

best_combination:
Built only from parts already in the four designs, by rate and idiom (tg128 with mul_mat_vec_q probed):
- **Every-thread counters on keys that decode** (constant, pid, SM, warp): route-first's sum cells, inline, with lane shards per cell. The measured anchors are 1531's add (0.010-0.015 ns) plus one strong load that is not yet measured.
  - Not device-table's unsharded word (about 1.06-1.17 ns, -51% to -65%).
  - Not host-cache's registered atomics (at least 59.8 ns).
- **Every-thread counters on keys that do not decode** (block ids, bins): shards' per-(SM, lane) insert-only tables (a lookup creates the key, adds only, relaxed loads), with the spill probe bounded. This replaces route-first's host call per operation (270-34,500 s per run).
- **Per-thread entry/exit scratch:** route-first's thread-private class in 1530 (+0.025 ns, measured analog). Not device-table's table (0.3-1.0 ns, 128 MiB at llama scale), and not host calls.
- **Store-shaped state at block or launch rate** (start_ts, cudagraph and gpu_shared_map leader state, self-aliased write-back): device-table's open-addressing table.
  - 8-byte strong stores, no lock;
  - a relaxed read of `bound` before reserving;
  - sharded loss counters;
  - an inline walk for constant fds.
  - Not route-first's word-cell lock, which costs 41-350 ns per operation when contended.
- **Per-launch counters:** any of the device paths above (at most 16-47 ms against today's 0.326 s). Host-cache's validated hit only for maps the CPU writes while kernels run, at launch rate.
- **Host call:** only a counted fallback, never the path for a per-thread case.

Two measurements decide this:
1. The dependent ld.relaxed.gpu.global on mul_mat_vec_q (shards check 1, route-first check 3).
2. The cost of ld.acquire.gpu's CCTL.IVALL on mul_mat_vec_q (device-table C3(c), run as a deciding variant).

scores.reasons:
Lens: fit and buildability. Tags: [code] = read in /home/jetson/src/bpftime-proto-70f7, [meas] = in our results, [inf] = my inference.

VERIFIED IN CODE
- Early return in route_thread_local_maps_of_module: `if (descs.empty() && sums.empty() && !device_arrays) return ptx;` (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1042) [code].
- MapBasicInfo is 40 B with no spare field and is defined twice: default_trampoline.cu:90-98 and nv_attach_impl.hpp:48-56 [code]. 1531 already stores its shard count in max_thread_count (sum_array_offset) [code].
- 1531's owner-pid CAS, cuMemAlloc + cuMemsetD8Async in relaxed capture mode, and the reference pin all exist and can be reused (nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:660-760; map_handler.cpp:1921ff) [code].
- Calling a trampoline .func from emitted probe PTX is feasible: probe functions already call `_bpf_helper_ext_000N`, and the trampoline is prepended to the same module [code].
- The patched module's `.target` is rewritten to the device's arch on both load paths: fatbin_record::compile_ptxs calls rewrite_ptx_target (nv_attach_fatbin_record.cpp:174), and the direct run uses wrap_ptx_with_trampoline_for_sm [code]. So `.relaxed.gpu`/CAS inline asm in an sm_61-built trampoline reaches ptxas as sm_87. Its compile-only check is the right gate.

WHAT IT REUSES
- From 1531: the shard formula, the measured red.global inline add path (0.010-0.015 ns per thread [meas]), key forwarding, sum_lookup's emitter style, allocation, owner rule and delivery schedule. This is the most direct reuse of 1531's measured code of the four.
- It fits the prototype's "shards are part of the design" (map-model-proto, What this means 3).
- Low memory [arith]: about 295 KB device for 1024 u64 entries, against 2 MiB for 1531 at 1024 entries.
- Hard constraints: everything is fixed at link instantiation, there is no per-launch step, graph replays work, and map_info is unchanged.

NEW WORK, larger than "reuse" suggests
- Delivery: registered_map holds a concrete `nv_gpu_device_array_map_impl*`, and deliver_locked copies word by word into host_words() with one snapshot entry (nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:186-200, 345-395) [code]. A map kind, a raw-copy kernel, the CPU merge and a host view with its own lock are new.
- Routing: today's provenance is register identity only. sum_ptrs takes registers whose every definition is an inlined sum lookup (nv_thread_local_routing.cpp:1259-1266), and guard_generic_atomics looks only at atom/red lines [code].
  - The "plain st refuses the probe" check is therefore new dataflow code.
  - As specified it is a denylist that admits escapes (stack spills, derived pointers).
  - The fail-closed allowlist pattern already exists in plan_by_value (nv_thread_local_routing.cpp:878-1010: every statement that mentions the lookup result must be on an allowlist) [code] and should be used instead.
- Refusal by fail() throws. route_thread_local_maps_of_module's caller catches it, and the whole patched file loads without probes (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1224-1240) [code]. One plain store in one probe therefore removes every probe of that module.

FIT LIMITS
- Coverage: it serves counters only, 4 of the 14 device-side example hash maps (survey).
- Existing tools declare HASH or 1501, so they reach this map only by editing their map type [code: gpu_map_type_without_cuda_ipc is unchanged].
- "Lookup creates the key" and "NOEXIST adds" remove the first-touch loss the tool's own idiom causes, by default. route-first treats the same effect as an opt-in the user decides (user rule: no repairing the tool's logic).
- No per-thread copies. The design states this and sends them to 1530/1532, which matches the model's division of labour.
- max_entries is enforced at merge, not at insert. Capacity is lifetime.
- One delivering process per map, as 1531.
- Size: 900-1,300 lines [inf, theirs]; plausible.
- It claims map type number 1533, as device-table does.
must_fix: Replace the denylist "plain st / non-64-bit add refuses the probe" with plan_by_value's allowlist (nv_thread_local_routing.cpp:878-1010): every statement that names a 1533 lookup-result register must be a null compare or a 64-bit atom/red at an in-value offset. Anything else, including a spill to the eBPF stack or a derived pointer (add/mov), refuses. Today's provenance (sum_ptrs, :1259-1266) is register identity only.

Refusal through fail() drops every probe of the patched file (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1224-1240 catch). Make the refusal per map instead: that map's calls in the offending function keep the trampoline helper with a counted -1/NULL, or the attach is rejected at load with the reason. Do not silently unpatch the module.

Delivery generalization: registered_map stores nv_gpu_device_array_map_impl* and deliver_locked writes host_words() word by word (nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:186-200, 345-395). Specify the map-kind interface, the second .entry in snapshot_ptx, and the merge lock against the syscall server's concurrent elem_lookup. Include them in the size estimate.

State to the user that existing examples need a map-type edit to use 1533. Present "lookup creates, NOEXIST adds" (which removes the idiom's first-touch loss) as a semantic the user approves, as route-first does with its fused counter.

Pick a type number that does not collide with device-table's 1533. Export the new find-or-insert .func as extern "C" in trampoline_ptx.h, and keep its compile-only SASS check (ATOMG.E.CAS.64.STRONG.GPU / LDG.E.64.STRONG.GPU) as a gate.

scores.reasons:
Lens: fit and buildability. Tags: [code] = read in /home/jetson/src/bpftime-proto-70f7, [meas] = in our results, [inf] = my inference.

VERIFIED IN CODE
- The 1501 -> 1533 swap fits at the caller, where the sizes are known (syscall_context.cpp:871-883 calls gpu_map_type_without_cuda_ipc with attr in hand) [code]. test_gpu_map_without_ipc.cpp:16-33 asserts 1501 -> 1, so it must change.
- map_info: extra_buffer and max_thread_count can carry the base and S with no struct change (create_map_basic_info, bpf_attach_ctx_cuda.cpp:510-571) [code].
- The trampoline's atomicCAS is `__nvvm_atom_cas_gen_i` (32-bit, generic, no .sem) (default_trampoline.cu:17-20) [code], so the 64-bit acquire CAS has to be inline asm, as claimed.
- Trampoline target: trampoline_ptx.h is `.version 8.1 / .target sm_61`, built with PTX_TARGET_ARCH ?= sm_61 (trampoline/Makefile) [code].
  - The claim that the patched module targets sm_87 holds: filter_out_version_headers_ptx keeps the first `.target` (core.cpp:165-180), and compile_ptxs rewrites it (nv_attach_fatbin_record.cpp:174) [code].
  - Its C2 compile check is the right gate.
- The existing atomic wrapper already sends any generic atomic with a global address to the `.global` form via its isspacep.global branch (nv_thread_local_routing.cpp:678-695) [code]. Program atomics on table values are covered once the pass runs.

WHAT IT REUSES
- 1531's allocation and zeroing, owner pid, reference pin, delivery thread, schedule, sync counting and relaxed capture mode.
- Helpers 1-3 as the only device entry point: nothing inline in v1, the least routing work of the three device-resident designs.
- It is the most general table: exact for loader-inserted counters, leader per launch, per-thread records (thread_mapping), per-thread start times and micro. This is the widest coverage of store-shaped idioms.
- Automatic for 1501. HASH needs an opt-in env var.
- Hard constraints are respected: fixed geometry, no per-launch step, works under graphs.

NEW WORK, larger than claimed
- Delivery: registered_map is typed to nv_gpu_device_array_map_impl* and copies word by word into host_words() (nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:186-200, 345-395) [code]. The versioned-read snapshot kernel, the two mirrors and the generation flip are new.
- "Traced 64-bit plain loads become ld.relaxed.gpu.global" is new dataflow. Today the pass rewrites only atom/red lines, and provenance is the register of an inlined lookup (:1259-1266) [code].
- Reading the update's value from the eBPF stack with 64-bit loads relies on 8-byte alignment of a generic local address, which probe-cost section 3 lists as not stated. Bytewise loads into registers avoid it.

FIT LIMITS
- Hot counters: about 1.0 ns per thread for one shared word [meas, merge-cost shape], about -64% projected on tg128 [inf]. v1 contradicts the prototype's own conclusion "Shards are part of the design, not an optimization" (map-model-proto README).
  - The fix (1534, sharded values at S x P x value_size) costs 4 MiB at 1024 u64 entries with P = 256 [arith]. That is not low memory.
- No per-thread copies.
- Per-thread pairing needs max_entries of at least the largest grid's distinct thread keys. That is grid-sized storage, against RD requirement 1 ("never by the grid"). Its own C5 rule pushes this case to 1530.
- CPU writes give EPERM after the device copy, as 1531 does. This changes behaviour for existing 1501 tools.
- One delivering process per map. Only 4-byte keys.
- Size: 900-1,300 lines [inf, theirs]; plausible.
must_fix: Make adds-only maps sharded in v1, not as a later variant. Either put the value at [slot][shard] in 1531's layout, reusing sum_array_offset and snapshot_ptx's shard sum (nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:128-180), or size P per map (per SM: 8). Otherwise every-thread counters ship at about 1.0 ns per thread [meas shape], against the prototype's "shards are part of the design".

Budget the routing dataflow as new code. In nv_thread_local_routing.cpp, provenance today is the register of an inlined sum lookup (:1259-1266), and guard_generic_atomics touches only atom/red. Converting traced plain loads, and logging 32-bit or plain stores, needs plan_by_value's allowlist pattern (:878-1010), extended to helper-1 call results (ld.param retval0), failing closed.

Generalize delivery: give registered_map a map kind, add a second .entry for the versioned-read snapshot, and add the mirror/generation flip (nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:186-200, 345-395). Specify how the syscall server's elem_lookup reads the active mirror into a per-thread buffer, because syscall_context.cpp:956-968 memcpys from the returned pointer after the call returns.

Spell out the HASH opt-in: the env var read by the server at syscall_context.cpp:871-883, and per-map or per-process scope. Update test_gpu_map_without_ipc.cpp:16-33. Document that existing 1501 tools now get EPERM on CPU writes after the device copy exists.

Read the update value from the eBPF stack without assuming 8-byte alignment of a generic local address (probe-cost section 3), e.g. bytewise into registers. Then store it with the 64-bit strong stores.
Choose a type number that does not collide with shards' 1533.

best_combination:
On fit and buildability, I checked the advisor's suggestion against the four designs: device-table's permanent key slots and shards' insert-only key words are the same mechanism.

**The shared mechanism**
- In both, a CAS-claimed 64-bit key word is never freed, sits in a cuMemAlloc table zeroed with cuMemsetD8Async (1531's code), uses linear probing, and has its CAS in the trampoline.
- Both need the same new delivery plumbing: a map kind in registered_map, a second snapshot .entry, and a CPU copy step (nv_gpu_model_maps.cpp:186-200, 345-395).
- So the largest reuse is one table path with two value layouts. It is not four mechanisms.

**Recommended parts**
1. **Key directory: device-table's, single device-wide.**
   - Header word with key and state, plus the `bound` counter, so max_entries is enforced at insert with E2BIG as in bpf. Shards enforces it only at merge.
   - Entry through helpers 1-3; constant-fd inlining comes later.
   - Automatic for 1501 at the syscall_context.cpp:871-883 caller. HASH by opt-in or a declared type.
2. **Adds-only value layout: 1531's [slot][shard] layout.**
   - This is device-table's 1534, and shards' rejected \"directory variant\".
   - It reuses sum_array_offset, the measured red.global inline add path (0.010-0.015 ns [meas]) and snapshot_ptx's shard sum almost unchanged. It keeps \"shards are part of the design\".
   - Memory is max_entries x S x 8 B, 2 KiB per u64 entry at S = 256 [arith]. If that is too much for \"low memory\", size S per map (per SM, S = 8: 64 B per entry, about +0.2 ns per thread on hot keys [meas merge-cost per-SM column]). Shards' per-shard tables (about 288 B per entry) cost a separate merge path.
3. **Store value layout: device-table's versioned words**, for leader-per-launch, per-thread records and other low-rate idioms. These are the idioms shards refuses.
4. **CPU view.**
   - For sums: shards' baseline trick (shown = D - B), so loaders can pre-insert, and CPU update, delete and lookup_and_delete work without writing device memory.
   - For store maps: EPERM after the device copy, as 1531.
5. **Routing.** One fail-closed use allowlist modelled on plan_by_value (nv_thread_local_routing.cpp:878-1010), shared by both layouts. Today's provenance is register identity only (:1259-1266). Run the pass when these maps exist (nv_attach_impl.cpp:1042).
6. **Per-thread scratch: 1530, by value.**
   - route-first's thread-private idea, but as a type the tool declares, not one inferred by a bytecode classifier. This keeps \"every thread its own copy\" at 8-16 B of local memory.
   - Leave route-first's classifier and its host-table upserts out of v1. The classifier has two ordering contradictions with the code (bpf_attach_ctx.cpp:642 before nv_attach_impl.cpp:214-229; map_handler.cpp:1252-1256 sizes HASH before any agent).
7. **Fallback: today's host call**, for keys other than 4 bytes, other value sizes, and maps not opted in.
   - Host-cache is not built. It is the dropped direction-2 scheme and serves no per-thread use.

**Gate before any build:** one compile-only check of the qualified inline PTX (CAS, acquire, release, fence.acq_rel.gpu) in the trampoline as built (sm_61 today; the patched module's .target is rewritten to sm_87 by nv_attach_fatbin_record.cpp:174), merged into the four llama.cpp modules, with registers compared per kernel.

scores.reasons:
Strongest documented core of the four. I checked its proofs against the board's PTX ISA 9.5 text.
- **One slot per key** [documented]. RMW atomicity (8.10.3, line 7593) with morally strong 64-bit .gpu CASes on one .global address (8.7) means only one CAS can claim an empty header. Once claimed, a slot's key never changes. A walk CASes every slot it reads as empty, so the claimed-at-a-and-b case cannot arise. Per-location SC (8.10.5) holds.
- **Value publication** [documented]: fence.acq_rel then a strong write is a release pattern (8.8, line 7405). It synchronizes with ld.acquire (8.9.4), and Coherence (8.10.1) stops an insert's store from erasing a later add. Its note that adds-only counters still need the acquire is right.
- **Versioned snapshot** [inference built correctly from 8.8/8.10.6].
- **Reserve before CAS.** `bound` is reserved before the claim CAS, so an E2BIG never rolls back a visible key. Route-first gets this wrong.
- **Inference is tagged honestly:** linearizability is not claimed, the C2 activemask result is respected, and the CAS lives in helpers (compiler.cpp:1690-1718 confirmed: the result register gets the pre-load).
- **Weak points:**
  - **Mixed-size hole logged, not refused.** Its own analysis says a 32-bit or plain tool access racing a 64-bit strong access voids every axiom in the program (8.7.2, line 7385: "The axioms ... do not apply if a PTX program contains one or more mixed-size data-races"). Map-lowering saw a u64 accessed as 2x32. The pass only logs these accesses, so its uniqueness and publication proofs fail open for the whole process. Yet idioms 7 and 8 (per-block start time, `*total += d`) are still served as 'approximate'.
  - **Waits under-cited.** The design cites only the §5.1 SIMT prose. CPG 5.9.2 (cpg-cuda-cpp-execution-model.txt:171-179) does document progress: once a device thread makes progress, all threads of its block eventually progress, and a thread that has executed a step gets concurrent forward progress. That covers waiting on a writer that has already done its CAS. It is a CUDA C++-level reading applied to inline PTX [inference], but it is better than 'no guarantee'.
  - **Mirror seqlock.** The writer bumps the generation with a release, then later writes the other buffer, with no fence before those writes. A slow reader that spans two deliveries can accept a torn copy [inference, C++ seqlock rule].
  - **Silent semantic changes for 1501 tools.** 1501 is converted to 1533 automatically. Those tools get, with no opt-in: capacity counting keys ever inserted, EPERM on CPU writes while running, waits, and -errno results. All are visible or counted, though.
  - Losses are counted (E2BIG, EEXIST, ENOENT, unstable slots). The status channel is still open.
- **Shared by all four:** 1531's zeroing chain and the claim-8 hand-over (P).
- **Not judged:** variant 1534 (not designed).
must_fix: Make the 32-bit/plain-access contract fail closed. Through a 1533 value pointer, refuse in the pass any 32-bit or plain access it cannot prove is ordered: same-thread program order, or after the acquire of the insert. Lower every traceable 64-bit access to a strong .gpu.global access, and refuse a pointer whose uses it cannot trace. By PTX 8.7.2, one mixed-size race voids the uniqueness and publication proofs for the whole process, so logging is not enough.

Stop serving idioms 7 (per-block start time written by every thread, read with plain loads) and 8 (`*total += d`) as 'approximate' unless C1 shows 64-bit accesses. Otherwise they are outside the model and must fall back (host call) or be refused.

Mirror seqlock: before writing the inactive mirror, the writer must make the new generation visible first (generation bump, then a release fence, then stores), and must write with relaxed atomic stores. Otherwise a reader that spans two deliveries can accept a torn value.

Cite CPG 5.9.2 (forward progress within a block; concurrent progress after a thread's first step) as the basis for waits, marked as a CUDA C++-level reading. Spinning must use atomic reads (device.threads.4).

scores.reasons:
Exact sums are on solid ground [documented]. Claims are atomic CASes, adds are morally strong `red.global` (8.7, 8.10.3), and the cuMemAlloc'd zeros reach all kernels through API synchronization (8.9.4). Any slot holding K is a valid add target, so %smid and %laneid only spread the adds. The quotes are verified (10.8/10.9 notes, CPG serialized atomics at cpg-legacy-12.9.txt:6811, the 5.7.4.3 'unsafe to rely upon' text). The delivery-monotonicity claim is honestly tagged [inference].

Where the device may hand a tool a wrong value without refusing (silent semantic changes):
- **Shard partials.**
  - A plain load returns the shard's partial sum, and the pass lowers it to `ld.relaxed.gpu.global`. It is served, not refused.
  - A fetch-add whose result is used returns the shard's old value. Ticket or index idioms (dir1 notes gpu_ext's launch queue needs one shared word) then get duplicates.
  - A value the loader wrote (B := D - V) reads back as 0 on the device.
- **Lookup creates the key.** A membership or filter lookup, where the CPU inserts keys the GPU tests, never returns NULL. No bpf interleaving gives that.
- **NOEXIST adds.** update(K,V,BPF_NOEXIST) returns 0 and adds. A set-once tool, such as the first timestamp per key, silently gets the sum of all threads' timestamps.

Access forms not covered:
- **32-bit loads.** It refuses 32-bit adds but is silent on 32-bit loads. If llvmbpf splits a u64 read into two `ld.u32` (map-lowering saw this), those race the 64-bit reds as a mixed-size race, and 8.7.2 voids the axioms for the whole program.
- **Escapes left as contracts** [design's own text]: a pointer spilled to the eBPF stack, and lookups with a non-constant fd served by the trampoline whose pointer uses are not traced. The pass has failed open twice before (map-lowering: 9+9 confirmed findings).

Other points:
- **First-touch loss.** It removes the loss the idiom causes by changing what the program observes, with no user decision flagged. Route-first marks the equivalent as opt-in.
- **max_entries is enforced at merge.** Which keys are shown depends on delivery timing. This is counted as 'keys not shown', so it is visible.
- **Refusals.** Where it does refuse, the refusal is fail-closed (fail() drops the module's probes, logged).
must_fix: Refuse (fail closed) every use of a 1533 value pointer except a null test and a 64-bit add whose result is unused. Plain loads and fetch-adds with a used result must be refused, or need an explicit per-map opt-in, because they silently return one shard's partial.
Refuse 32-bit and other narrower loads through value pointers. Today they are not addressed, and with 64-bit red they form a mixed-size race that voids the PTX axioms for the whole program (8.7.2).

Make update(BPF_NOEXIST)-as-add and lookup-creates-the-key apply only where the pass proves the counter idiom (the NOEXIST insert sits on the lookup's NULL branch, with the same key and the value it adds). Otherwise refuse, so set-once and membership uses do not silently get sums or non-NULL lookups.
Close the escapes instead of leaving contracts: refuse probes where a value pointer is spilled to the stack, and refuse lookups with a non-constant fd, or trace their uses too.
State that removing the first-touch loss is a change in what the program observes (lookup never returns NULL), and leave it to the user, as route-first does for its fused counter.

scores.reasons:
It has the right philosophy and the most careful exactness criterion: a result must be bpf-legal under some interleaving that CUDA permits.
- **Fail-closed by design.**
  - The classifier works on eBPF bytecode, defaults to Top or refusal, and freezes its decision. A later attach that does not fit is refused.
  - Sum cells refuse reads.
  - Word cells hand out private copies, so the tool's 2x32-bit accesses never race a shared cell. Of the four designs, this is the only one that removes the mixed-size hole.
  - Inference is tagged throughout. Quotes are verified (PTX 5.1.5 line 3178, 10.1 line 46004, guide 3.2 line 1995, 4.2.8.2 line 3200).
- **Concrete exactness violations in its own protocols:**
  1. **Sum-cell insert order.** The insert CASes state 0->1, then reserves occupancy, and undoes both on E2BIG. Lookups treat state 1 as present. Adds made during the claimed window stay in the shards after the rollback, and a racing NOEXIST got -EEXIST for a key that ends absent. Neither outcome is bpf-legal [reasoned from the text].
  2. **Fetch result ignores base.** With S=1, the claim that 'fetch-add returns the old value as bpf does' ignores base. After a prefill (base = value) or a CPU write (base := v - S), the device returns the raw shard sum, not the logical value.
  3. **CPU flag checks against a stale table.** CPU writes decide EEXIST/ENOENT against the host table at once, then reach the device only at the next delivery. A GPU NOEXIST of the same key before that delivery also succeeds: two successful NOEXIST inserts. The behaviour when the pending ring is full is unspecified.
  4. **Atomics on private copies.** Word cells route atomics on the private snapshot through isspacep.local plain RMW, and the design claims pt_hash RMW is served exactly. With all 32 lanes holding the same snapshot, each warp writes back v+1. I could not construct that outcome under bpf, where the adds land atomically in the shared element and each update copies an element that already holds them [inference]. The design's interleaving argument covers plain stores, not atomics. It says it keeps today's 'about half' loss, but this would likely lose about 31 of 32.
  5. **Fence missing in the lock path.** The word-cell update text has no fence between the lock CAS and the value stores. Its own seqlock argument needs one.
- **Thread-private entries rest on schedule reasoning** [inference]: blocks may run in series (guide 3.2). That argument is per map and does not compose with the program's other shared maps: a joint outcome may need a cycle no serial schedule explains. Cooperative launches break it and are undetected, so that case fails open.
- **The classifier itself is unreviewed.** It is the single point of failure.
must_fix: Sum cells: reserve occupancy before the state CAS (as device-table does), and give the reservation back if the CAS loses. Never return a pointer while state is 1, or never roll back a state other threads may have observed. Otherwise E2BIG leaves adds and EEXISTs for a key that never existed.
Allow S=1 fetch-with-result only on maps with no prefill and no CPU writes (base is identically 0), or apply base on the device. Otherwise the returned old value is not the value bpf would return.

CPU writes to cell keys while kernels run: decide EEXIST/ENOENT/E2BIG against device state under the cell lock, or return EPERM while a device copy exists (as 1531/1532 and device-table do). Deciding against the lagging host table allows two successful NOEXIST inserts. Specify what happens when the pending ring is full (refuse, never drop).
Word cells: do not serve atomics through the pointer (pt_hash RMW) with a plain RMW on a private copy. Send such maps to the host-call hash unless the per-warp outcome is shown to be bpf-legal.
Word-cell update: add fence.acq_rel.gpu after the lock CAS and before the value stores in the operations text, as the seqlock argument requires.

Thread-private class: hook or refuse cooperative launches (the serial-schedule argument fails there). Admit the class only when the program's other maps cannot contradict a serial block schedule, or state that the argument is per map and not proven.

scores.reasons:
The best at keeping eBPF hash semantics. The CPU table stays the only owner. The device answers only where the answer is provably one the host would give:
- a validated hit, where the word is equal so the element is still in the same life holding the same key;
- NOEXIST on a validated present key.

Everything else stays a synchronous host call, errors are -1 as today, and the CPU view is unchanged. Its claims check out against the code (bpftime_hash_map.hpp): the word is at offset 0, retire stores (w & ~USED) + 2 with release (line 486), link_locked stores w|USED with release (line 505), elements never move, and the check-to-use window matches the kernel's prealloc window. The §5.8.3 quote and the membar quote (ptx 26363) are verified, and it is right to read membar's 'performed' as real time only by inference.

Defects:
1. **ref = 0 window.** Entry publication releases PUBLISHED before `ref` is stored, so a reader can see ref = 0 = (word 0, index 0). The table buffer is zero-filled (`buffer.resize(total, 0)`), so a never-used element 0 has word 0. Validation then passes and returns a pointer into a free element for a key that may be absent: a wrong result [code read].
2. **Miss reuse.** The operations publish ABSENT|seq+1 after the response, while the concurrency argument needs the bump before the host call. With the bump after, a call that started after the other lane's lookup (and after a CPU insert of that key) can still return NULL.
3. **Lane loop.** Lanes answered on the device and host-call lanes are mixed in the `__syncwarp(__activemask())` turn loop. Agreement on that mask is not documented (C5 claim 9 NF) and was violated in C2. The design lists this as a risk only.
4. **Start-up rule.** The rule 'disable unless CAN_USE_HOST_POINTER... equals the value assumed' is ambiguous, and the Orin reports 0 (feasibility attrs.out.txt). C5's alias rule needs 'one device pointer per segment', not the attribute equal to 1.

What is documented and what is not:
- 'Documented in-process' holds only on C5's per-object CUDA C++ reading (§5.8.3), and for a libcu++ atomic_ref form. A hand-written ld.acquire.sys rests on prose (C5 claim 4 note).
- The tool's bpf() writer is another process, so P (claim 8), as today.

The first-touch loss narrows but stays. It is bpf-legal and counted.

Not judged (not designed): the sum extension, GPU-run writers, fused lookup-or-insert.
must_fix: Validation must require the in-use bit (w & 1) and treat ref = 0 as invalid, or store ref before releasing PUBLISHED. As specified, a reader can validate (word 0, index 0) against a never-used, zero-filled element 0 and return a pointer for a key that may be absent.

Same-call miss reuse: publish PENDING/seq+1 before the host lookup is issued (as the concurrency argument assumes), not after the response. Otherwise NULL can be answered for a lookup that started after the miss was served, and after a CPU insert.

Keep every lane on one documented path in host_call. Either all lanes pass through the turn loop, with device-answered lanes skipping only the request, or a mask known by construction replaces `__activemask()`. Mixing early-returning lanes into `__syncwarp(__activemask())` is NF (C5 claim 9), and C2 measured millions of violations.

Rewrite the start-up rule as 'all GPU code uses the one pointer from cuMemHostGetDevicePointer' (C5 alias rule). The Orin reports CAN_USE_HOST_POINTER_FOR_REGISTERED_MEM = 0, so a rule requiring 1 would disable the cache. Write the validation load as cuda::atomic_ref<uint32_t, thread_scope_system>::load(acquire), so the in-process case rests on §5.8.3 rather than on prose.

best_combination:
For correctness, combine as follows:
- **Default path.** host-cache's CPU-owned table, with validated hits and the host call as the fail-closed fallback, applies to any map or access no proof admits. It keeps bpf semantics nearly unchanged.
- **Device core.** device-table's claim protocol: reserve capacity, then CAS permanent key slots; acquire walks; fence then release publish; versioned snapshot; all CAS inside helpers. Admit a map only where route-first's bytecode classifier (Top or refusal by default, decision frozen per map) proves the access pattern.
- **Non-atomic accesses: refuse, never log.** Plain reads and stores through value pointers either go to private copies (route-first's word-cell snapshot, only for plain read-modify-write written back with update, never for atomics) or are refused. Adds-only per-(SM, lane) shards (shards / 1531's contract) are used only when the classifier proves null tests plus unused-result 64-bit adds. No shard partial is ever readable on the device.
- **CPU writes while kernels run return EPERM** (1531/device-table). Do not use route-first's queued rebase or the shards view arithmetic, both of which decide flags against stale state.
- **Losses** (E2BIG, EEXIST, unstable slots, fallbacks) are counted and delivered through a status channel.
- **User opt-ins only:** semantic changes that remove the idiom's own first-touch loss (shards' lookup-creates and NOEXIST-as-add, route-first's fused counter) stay explicit opt-ins for the user to decide.
